title: Edge Computing Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Offline execution, device constraints, synchronization, and local inference at the edge. The Edge Computing Database documents computing at the network's edge — on devices, gateways, and local servers where connectivity is unreliable, power is limited, and latency matters. Records cover offline-first execution patterns, device constraint budgets (CPU, RAM, battery, thermals), edge-cloud synchronization strategies, and local inference deployment. The cloud is a convenience; the edge is where the physical world meets compute.

title: Edge Computing Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Constraints: compute (weak CPUs, optional NPUs), memory (MBs to GBs), power (battery/milliwatt budgets), thermals (no fans, throttling), connectivity (intermittent, metered). Patterns: local-first (work offline, sync opportunistically); store-and-forward (queue operations, replay on connect); edge caching (hot data local, cold in cloud); split inference (light model on device, heavy in cloud when connected). Sync: CRDTs for mergeable data; last-write-wins with vector clocks where acceptable; manual review queues for conflicts that matter. Budgets: per device class, record {cpu_mips, ram_mb, power_mw, thermal_headroom}; inference must fit with margin. Updates: signed OTA with rollback; staged rollouts.

title: Edge Computing Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: budget test (over-budget workloads rejected); sync test (all queued operations apply after outage); conflict test (CRDT merges converge); determinism test. Limitations: device classes evolve — recheck envelopes; real fleets need device management; security review per deployment. Every record names its device class and measurement date.
